observation.visible_scene: A wide, eye-level landscape shot of a rugged, snow-capped mountain range rising above a calm lake. The slopes are covered in tan/brown tussock grass and dark low shrubs, with a thin band of forest along the far shoreline. The lake surface acts as a near-mirror, reflecting the mountains and the dark treeline in deep green tones. In the immediate foreground there is a strip of dry pale grass with a small evergreen bush cluster at the lower left and a single grass tuft at the bottom center. The sky is a flat, overcast white.
visible_changes: The camera framing is fixed throughout the excerpt: the left snow patch, the mountain ridgeline, the horizontal shoreline, the foreground grass strip and the left bush cluster occupy the same pixel positions in the first and last frames, indicating no pan, tilt, zoom or translation.
No discrete objects (people, animals, vehicles, birds) enter, leave, or move within the frame; the scene contains no tracked moving subject.

The only perceptible variation is extremely subtle and confined to the water's reflective surface and the foreground grass tuft: faint, slow shimmer/texture shifts in the mirror reflection and negligible sway of the dry grass, consistent with light wind or gentle surface ripples rather than any large motion.
No editing cut or seam is visible inside the segment; the view is continuous from t=0.000 s to t=1.333 s.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the water's surface motion is stronger or weaker outside this 1.3-second window, and whether any larger event (a boat, an animal, a person) occurs before or after this crop.
The actual wind conditions and the time of day, which are not directly observable from the still-looking frames.
uncertain_details: The minute differences in the reflection texture and grass shape between frames are at the limit of visibility and could be video compression noise rather than genuine physical motion; the shot is effectively static.
It is not possible to confirm from these frames whether the foreground grass is actually swaying or simply rendered slightly differently frame to frame.

Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
